title: Strong Spades, uncertain side winners

feedback.title: A measured raise
feedback.summary: Four Spades is a plausible plan, but two Aces do not guarantee four tricks.
points: Control: the Spade Ace is your top trump; the Diamond Ace is a likely side winner if opponents can follow.
Probable, not safe: extra Spade tricks need promotion or useful ruffs; four trumps alone do not secure four tricks.
Risk: the Heart King can lose to the Ace, and the Diamond Queen is conditional.

feedback.title: Sans needs more established winners
feedback.summary: Four Sans is legal, but it gives up ruffing opportunities while your side honors remain conditional.
points: Control: you hold two Aces, but no long sequence of established winners.
Probable: the Diamond Queen and Heart King need favorable play or distribution.
Risk: Spades headed by Ace-Jack still lack King-Queen control; Sans does not turn the low cards into winners.

feedback.title: Five relies on several things going well
feedback.summary: Your four Spades give a direction, but five tricks needs too much help from conditional cards.
points: Control: two Aces provide the clearest starting point.
Probable: a promoted Spade or a ruff may add a trick, but neither is established now.
Risk: counting the Heart King and Diamond Queen as certain winners overstates the hand.

feedback.title: The target outruns the visible strength
feedback.summary: 5 Hearts asks more of this hand than its controls support.
points: King-seven is only a doubleton, and North has already bid Hearts. This is a fragile trump base.
The Heart King and Diamond Queen remain conditional; neither is a guaranteed extra trick.
A lower legal target is more defensible. This assessment does not predict the exact deal outcome.
